title: WearSurfacesDatasets: how surfaces change as they wear

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How does a piece of cardboard look after it's been rubbed with sandpaper for two and a half meters? This dataset has the measured answer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Real ones. It publishes surface textures captured during controlled wear tests, organized by material, abrasive grit, load and sliding distance. It's the public dataset from Antoine's ÉTS master's research on wear in texture space, for graphics and tribology researchers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Each measured state stores a set of maps, like height, bump and normal maps, as images inside a Parquet file. The page lists twenty wear timelines, from cardboard at five different loads to foam, MDF, PLA and soft wood.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Scripts to pack and extract the data, and an alignment pipeline that registers each sequence, adds interpolated steps and extrapolates future normal maps. There's also a WebGPU viewer in the browser where you scrub through the distance or press play to watch the wear progress.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The full write-up has the viewer walkthrough.
